items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: For instance, playing with Tommy Dorsey was a great experience. But that was almost a terrorizing experience in many ways, because Tommy was bigger than life and he could fire you at a drop of a hat you know.

ctx.x: A good promoter, and Basie will tell you the same thing. I’ll tell you working with Count Basie was like, we were a family, it was actually a family. As loyal as a family, maybe more so. And it was one of the happiest experiences of my whole career. For instance, playing with Tommy Dorsey was a great experience. But that was almost a terrorizing experience in many ways, because Tommy was bigger than life and he could fire you at a drop of a hat you know. He was generous, he was, and I’ll quote Zoot Sims, you may…
Was there ever a problem with the racial mix in that group?

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah, three times I went with Tommy.

ctx.x: So you just kept kind of coming back?
Yeah, three times I went with Tommy. So that Boyd Raeburn experience probably was from California to New York.
I still can’t get my arms around that idea of not having a home base and just being with the band and on, you know, on the bus.
